textbookText: Section 'D' Long answer type questions. 1. The given figure shows the laboratory preparation of ammonia gas. Answer the following question after observing the given figure. a) Write the balanced chemical reaction of laboratory preparation of ammonia gas by this method. Ans:- The balanced chemical reaction of laboratory preparation of ammonia gas by this method is 2NH₄Cl(s) + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCl₂ (s) + 2H₂O (l) + 2NH₃(g). b) Why the mouth of hard glass test tube is inclined downward? Ans:- The mouth of the hard glass test tube is inclined downward to prevent the condensed water formed during the reaction from flowing back into the hot part of the test tube and cracking it. c) Ammonia gas cannot be collected over water. Why? Ans:- Ammonia gas cannot be collected over water because it is highly soluble in water and readily dissolves in it. d) Why color/type of litmus paper can help to confirm that the gas jar is filled with ammonia gas? Ans:- Ammonia gas is basic in nature and forms ammonium hydroxide in the presence of moisture, which turns moist red litmus paper blue, thus confirming the presence of ammonia gas. 2. Draw a neat diagram of the laboratory preparation of carbon dioxide gas and label any two parts. Also write the balanced chemical equation involved in this process. What happen when carbon dioxide gas is passed into lime water for a short period? Ans: The labelled diagram of the laboratory preparation of carbon dioxide gas is given below, The balanced chemical equation involved in this process is CaCO₃ (s) + 2HCl (aq) → CaCl₂ (aq) + H₂O (l) + CO₂ (g). When carbon dioxide gas is passed into lime water for a short time, lime water turns milky due to the formation of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃). 3. Study the given diagram and answer the following questions: i) Which gas is being collected in gas jar? Ans:- Ammonia gas is being collected in gas jar. ii) Which coloured litmus paper is used to identify such gas? Ans:- Ammonia gas is basic in nature so we use moist red litmus paper to identify such gas. It turns into blue. iii) Why does this gas is collected in inverted gas jar? Ans:- Ammonia gas is collected in an inverted gas jar because it is lighter than air and rises upward, so it is collected by downward displacement of air. iv) What happens when lime tower is not used to collect such gas? Ans:- If a lime tower is not used, the ammonia gas collected will be moist and impure because it will contain water vapour and acidic impurities, as quicklime in the lime tower is used to dry the ammonia gas.
